summary: Bruno Snell was a scholar of linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1919–1920), the University of Göttingen (~1920–1922), and the University of Oxford (~1921–1922), and held a post at the University of Hamburg (~1925–1975).

Bryan D. Lowe specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University and under mentors including Jacqueline I. Stone, Martin Collcutt, and Toru Funayama. He was attested as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Vanderbilt University (2017–2019).

Bryan J. Cuevas is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Emory University under Donald Phillip Verene and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He held posts at Princeton and Florida State University.
Bryan W. Van Norden specializes in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Stanford University (~1985–1991) and held the James Monroe Taylor Chair in Philosophy at Vassar College (~1997).

Bryce Ryan worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Washington and Harvard University, and later taught at Iowa State, Rutgers, the University of Ceylon (~1948–1952), Cornell, Wayne State, and the University of Miami (1957–1976).

Buddhadeb Gorai is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He earned an M.A. at Jadavpur University (2006–2008), served as an assistant professor at Deshbandhu College for Girls (2014), and founded the Bhāratāyana IKS Journal as editor-in-chief (2026).

Buddhike Indrasena works in Indology and medicine. Educated at the University of Peradeniya, the Postgraduate Institute of Medicine, and other institutions, he served as a consultant surgeon at several Sri Lankan hospitals and as a Medical Statistician Associate at the World Academy of Medical Leadership.
Buddhodev Ghosh works in Indology and philosophy. He held positions at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (2022) and the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (2024–2025).

Bulcsu Siklós specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles R. Bawden, and held an attested post at SOAS University of London in 1996.

Bunga Fukui was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Max Kaltenmark, and Rolf Alfred Stein, later serving as professor at Waseda University (~1978–2004).

Bunkyo Aoki worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University and under Kozui Otani (~1910–1914), and was appointed a lecturer in Tibetan at the University of Tokyo in 1951, succeeding Tokan Tada.

Bunsaku Kurata specialized in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda University, held multiple roles at the National Commission for Protection of Cultural Properties, and became Director of Nara National Museum in 1975.

Bunyiu Nanjio worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He studied at Otani University and the University of Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and served as director of Otani University.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz, he held posts at Rikkyo University, the First Higher School, and Kyoto University, where he served as professor and president.

Burchard Brentjes was a scholar of archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Heinz Mode (1947–1952) and held a post there from ~1960 to 1978, succeeding Mode.

Burkard Wilhelm Leist specialized in legal history and Indology. He studied at Göttingen, Heidelberg, and Berlin under Friedrich Carl von Savigny, and held professorships of law at the universities of Basel (1846), Rostock (1847), and Jena (1853).

Burkhard Quessel is a scholar of Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was attested as a member in 1997, and was attested as a curator at the British Library between 2002 and 2012.

Burmansah Burmansah works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Universitas Komputer Indonesia (2004–2008) and the State University of Jakarta (2014–2016), and was appointed a lecturer at STIAB Jinarakkhita in 2020.

Burton Stein was a historian working in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Illinois Chicago and the University of Chicago, and held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1965–1983) and SOAS University of London (1983).

Burton Watson was a scholar of sinology and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Kyoto University, later holding posts at Doshisha University, Kyoto University, Columbia University (1961), and Stanford University (~1964–1965).
